module_title: The 4 Phases of the Business Cycle and Basic Concepts
introduction: The periodic ups and downs in a nation's economic activity (GDP, employment, and production) form the Business Cycle. At this beginner level, we will understand the four core phases of this cycle and the difference between simple growth and true development.

core_concepts.title: 1. Expansion (Boom / Recovery)
core_concepts.description: This is the phase where the economy is growing. Production (GDP) is rising, employment opportunities are increasing, people's incomes are going up, and overall consumer demand in the market is strong.

core_concepts.title: 2. Peak
core_concepts.description: This is the highest point of the business cycle. The economy is operating at its maximum capacity. At this point, prices (Inflation) rise rapidly because the massive demand in the market begins to exceed the available supply of goods.

core_concepts.title: 3. Contraction (Recession)
core_concepts.description: Following the peak, the economy begins to cool down. Consumer demand falls, production decreases, and companies begin layoffs to cut costs, leading to a sharp rise in unemployment.

core_concepts.title: 4. Trough
core_concepts.description: This is the lowest point of the business cycle. Economic activity hits rock bottom. After hitting the trough, the economy eventually begins a new phase of 'Recovery' (Expansion), and the cycle starts all over again.

important_entities.title: Economic Growth vs. Economic Development
important_entities.significance: Economic Growth is strictly 'Quantitative' (a simple increase in the real GDP). Economic Development is 'Qualitative'; it includes GDP growth PLUS improvements in the standard of living, reduction in poverty, and better healthcare and education (measured by the Human Development Index - HDI).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Technical Definition of a Recession
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common exam question: 'When is an economy technically considered to be in a recession?' Answer: An economy is in a technical recession when its Real GDP registers negative growth (shrinks) for 'Two Consecutive Quarters' (i.e., a continuous 6-month period).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Expansion -> Peak -> Contraction -> Trough. Memorize this sequence.

exam_strategy_tips: Examiners often ask: 'In which phase of the business cycle is inflation generally the highest?' The answer is always the 'Peak'.
